job.rawJd:
General recruiter and networking profile, not an employer posting.

Target: healthcare and pharmaceutical agency account management, client strategy, and adjacent client-services roles.

Core work: own client relationships; manage budgets, briefs, timelines, national broadcast and integrated campaign delivery, cross-functional teams, FDA preclearance, and med-legal and MLR review; use research and campaign performance to guide client recommendations.

Resume architecture: use the March 2015 account-management resume as the primary content source. Give direct account work the most space. Keep every later employer and date visible, but retain only the recent bullets that strengthen client discovery, stakeholder alignment, regulated delivery, recommendations, or team leadership.

This package must be fit-gated again against each employer's actual job description before application.

classification.primarySource: The March 2015 account-management resume is the main content source. It directly proves account ownership across pharma and consumer brands, $2M-$50M+ budgets, national television launches, FDA and med-legal review, digital and loyalty programs, vendor coordination, and junior account oversight.
classification.supportingSource: The current resume and portfolio supply the later chronology and selected proof of client discovery, regulated workflows, presentation-ready recommendations, and cross-functional leadership. Those roles support the story but do not receive equal weight.

resume.summary: Healthcare account leader looking to make a return to account management after 7+ years with Fortune 500 pharma and consumer brands. I managed $2M-$50M+ budgets and led broadcast, digital, social, CRM, print, and unbranded programs through FDA and med-legal review. Later work in UX, analytics, and AI taught me what delivery teams need from the account lead and where client work tends to get stuck.
